title: Building Lumina with Claude/Codex — could use some help getting the combat feel right
author: zer0proof
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’ve been working on Lumina, a 3D bullet heaven / roguelite in Unity, with a lot of help from Claude and Codex. I could use some outside eyes on the visuals and combat feel, and some advice from people using AI on their own games.

The workflow has mostly been to describe a specific change, have the agents work on the C# scripts and Unity scene through MCP, rebuild the web version, then play it and send back screenshots or clips of what feels off. I’m choosing the assets, directing the design and playtesting. The art is a mix of licensed/CC0 packs and some AI-generated assets.

The part I keep struggling with is that satisfying bullet heaven feel. I want colorful attacks and weapons spinning around the player, with upgrades that visibly change the action. Earlier versions had plenty of flash, but there were circles inside circles and it got hard to read. We cleaned that up and improved the effects and animations, and then some of the excitement disappeared.

I’ve bought more art, animation and VFX packs, which have helped, but I’m learning how much still depends on timing, scale, color and hit feedback. Swapping in a better-looking effect doesn’t automatically make the whole fight feel better. Balance is another thing I’m still tuning; some builds have let me practically stand still once everything is upgraded.

If you try it or watch the trailer, what would you change first? Where does it need more impact, and where is there still too much going on? Also, how do you get useful results from an AI agent when your feedback is basically “it works, but it doesn’t feel right yet”?

Free desktop browser build: [https://zeroproof.itch.io/lumina](https://zeroproof.itch.io/lumina)

30-second trailer: [https://youtu.be/qX8xfHtIgJw](https://youtu.be/qX8xfHtIgJw)

Honest criticism, workflow suggestions and examples worth studying would all help.
